note: Deliberate exceptions to the reachability gate. Every entry needs a date and a reason; the gate refuses to run when either is missing. TWO MECHANICS A LATER EDIT MUST KNOW, both recorded here because this file is the artifact a re-seed touches. (1) AN ENTRY EXEMPTS EXACTLY ONE ROW. The gate reduces a row key to `kind<TAB>subject` (`check-reachability.mjs:1612` `allowlistKey`) and compares it for equality against each entry's `key` (`:1599-1600`); there is no wildcard, prefix or class key. An entry keyed on a representative row is therefore a dated ADJUDICATION of a class, not an exemption covering it — the class's other members are accepted through `scripts/audit/reachability-baseline.json`, and repairing one of them warns only about the single row the entry names. The entries dated 2026-09-17 that say "one class of N rows" are all of this kind. (2) LINE ENDINGS. This file and `reachability-baseline.json` are CRLF on disk with no BOM, while `--seed-baseline` WRITES LF. A re-seed therefore leaves the baseline LF and produces a whole-file EOL diff against the CRLF convention; re-normalise both files to CRLF after any re-seed and re-run `--gate` and `--digest` to confirm the tool's behaviour is unchanged. Committed blobs are LF under `core.autocrlf=true`, so this is a working-tree rule, not a content rule. Recorded for the milestone record: it belongs in `docs/handoff/2026-09-15-m2-reachability-gate-handoff.md` §6 ("Three traps a later edit will hit") as a third trap, where Task 3 landed it on 2026-09-17 — flagged to Task 3, which owns that document.

entries.reason: `by-design`, because all three parts of the Phase A characterisation were wrong: `createUnifiedSpillStore` (`packages/output-retention/src/spill-guard.ts:90-92`) is a three-line root-selecting factory that **never calls GC**; GC **is** wired at `spill-guard.ts:25` inside `createOutputSpillGuard`, which production mounts at `packages/session-executor/src/assembly.ts:524` whenever a host passes `outputSpill` (`assembly.ts:129`); and **no production host passes one**, so what ships is **no spill store at all** — the shell path's default retention is `opts.shellRetention ?? { maxBytes: 64_000 }` (`assembly.ts:400`), which carries no `spill` key (`packages/shell/src/index.ts:135` declares it, `:280` tests it), and nothing outside `test/` ever passes either option with a value (`apps/cli/src/run.ts:252,288` only forwards what its caller gave). The decision is the source's own, at `packages/output-retention/src/index.ts:170-171`: *"絕不寫 workspace——研究決策；**不清理（已知 limitation）**"*, and the guard, the GC it calls and the factory landed together in `c3875a9`. Follow-up: **none owed in code** — if a host ever supplies a spill root it gets exactly the GC wired at `:25`, so the honest future question is retention **policy** (age/size caps), not wiring.

First, the function is a **process-global destroyer**: `packages/session-query/src/index.ts:51-54` holds a module-level `Set` (`:51` `const openConnections = new Set<DatabaseSync>()`, `:52` `export function closeSessionQueries()`, `:53-54` close-and-clear), so any caller reaching it closes every other caller's handles too — and a **second, independent** such set now exists at `packages/session-query/src/file-backed.ts:90` with its own `closeFileBackedConnections()` at `:91`, so "the connection set" is two sets at HEAD, not one. Second, the honest long-term fix is a **per-instance `close()`** — which adds a member to the published `SessionQuery` interface (`:43-46`, re-opened: `:43` the interface, `:44-45` its two methods) and is therefore **M**: a public-surface change with its own spec, not a wiring gap. **Measured while re-opening this cell:** `closeFileBackedConnections` (`file-backed.ts:91`) is exported and re-exported by the package entry, and `closeSessionQueries` does call it at `packages/session-query/src/index.ts:55` — so the composition **inside** the package is wired. What is missing is any caller: measured by grep over `packages/*/src` and `apps/cli/src`, the only occurrences of either name are the two declarations, that one in-package call, the entry's re-export and two comments, so **neither function is reached from a production path**. That is the same wiring gap this row describes, not a refutation of it.
